profile.bio: Ashutosh Pal Singh. Security analyst in vulnerability management and threat detection, MSc Cyber Security Engineering (University of Warwick), Microsoft SC-200 certified. These projects measure the error rates behind blockchain investigations and forensic timelines. Based in the UK, open to roles in blockchain analytics and crypto investigations, DFIR, fraud and financial crime, SOC, vulnerability management and security research.

projects.title: evm-cluster-check
projects.oneLine: How often published Ethereum clustering and taint rules link addresses that belong to two different exchanges, and what causes it.
projects.headline: On 3 days of Ethereum (5.44M transactions), naive deposit-address reuse merged 198 pairs of addresses from two different exchanges, none caused by poisoning, sweepers or fee services; the same-sender rule merged 359, and 60% of those came only through poisoning transfers.

misses: Binance and Bitstamp publish their reserve lists only on their own sites, which I could not reach, so every false merge count is a lower bound.
Only one free provider served Ethereum logs, so the token transfer data has no second source. chain-evidence checked 40 blocks of it instead.
The taint stage ran the machine out of memory and lost a run. It now keeps one slim table and resumes from saved stages.
The 20 sampled false merges were classified by script, not opened one by one on a block explorer.

projects.title: timetruth
projects.oneLine: Scripted actions at known times, then a check of whether mainstream forensic tools report those times correctly.
projects.headline: 1828 tool-reported times checked (16 runs: 4 file systems x 4 time-zone scenarios x 30 actions, 6 tool configurations). 502 (27%) were not the true instant: 264 wrong value, 146 right clock reading in the wrong zone, 76 ambiguous, 16 missing.

proof.label: of forensic tool times were not the true instant

misses: libfaketime also shifted stat() results, so my first NTFS run applied the offset twice. Fixed with NO_FAKE_STAT=1.
MFTECmd would not run under Mono, so analyzeMFT stands in on Linux and is labelled that way everywhere.
Every image was written by a Linux driver. The Windows kit that would test real Windows writes has not been run yet.
ext4 ignores libfaketime, so the ext4 "DST" runs did not actually cross a clock change.

projects.title: chain-evidence
projects.oneLine: Ask several independent providers for the same on chain data, flag any disagreement, and prove completeness against the block header.
projects.headline: Across 524 finalised Ethereum block ranges asked of three free RPC providers, every recent range agreed (383/383), but on older blocks a provider silently returned nothing where receipt proofs show 286 logs (2/20 comparable ranges), and publicnode returned `null` receipts for 7/7 sampled transactions older than ~6 days.

metrics.label: ethereum: empty successes (0 logs where logs exist)
ethereum/drpc: blocks whose receipts reproduce receiptsRoot

proof.label: silent empty answers where receipt proofs show logs

misses: I deleted the bundle of the first silent empty answer while resetting results. It is recorded in my notes and not counted.
1rpc ran out of free quota and relays publicnode, so most Ethereum comparisons are only two way.
My first probe said publicnode serves deep receipts. It counted a null answer as success.
mainnet.base.org refuses eth_getLogs, so Base has receipt proofs but no log comparison.

out: On 3 days of Ethereum (5.44M transactions), naive deposit-address reuse merged 198 pairs of addresses from two different exchanges, none caused by poisoning, sweepers or fee services; the same-sender rule merged 359, and 60% of those came only through poisoning transfers.

1828 tool-reported times checked (16 runs: 4 file systems x 4 time-zone scenarios x 30 actions, 6 tool configurations). 502 (27%) were not the true instant: 264 wrong value, 146 right clock reading in the wrong zone, 76 ambiguous, 16 missing.

Across 524 finalised Ethereum block ranges asked of three free RPC providers, every recent range agreed (383/383), but on older blocks a provider silently returned nothing where receipt proofs show 286 logs (2/20 comparable ranges), and publicnode returned `null` receipts for 7/7 sampled transactions older than ~6 days.
